scope: Indexing the derived queue in chunks (app/stories.py refresh_derived, _refresh_chunk; app/ranking.py rebuild_clusters)
environment: macOS isolated copies of the titles-v4 rehearsal index (perf6: 89,575 items, 57,924 story memberships), schema 55, titles-v5 matcher; no network, no model calls
problem: A matcher, topic or watchlist change queues every item, and one refresh indexed the whole queue in one write transaction: 257 s on the rehearsal data, while other writers give up after a 30 s busy timeout.
design: refresh_derived() takes the queue earliest first, 1,500 items per transaction (REFRESH_CHUNK); each chunk commits on its own and later chunks see earlier ones as indexed. A chunk stops taking items after 12 s (REFRESH_CHUNK_SECONDS), a guard for very slow hosts only.

Items indexed by an earlier chunk of the same refresh are not queued again because their event's anchor or former anchor is still queued; a chunk made only of such items (edited again by another writer) ends the refresh and leaves them queued.

Each chunk's window also spans every member of the events its items belong to, so a rechecked member of a merged event reaching past 72 h still finds its anchor and former anchors (this also affected incremental refreshes).
The refresh after each crawl indexes one chunk; a backlog is worked off by the AI job's refresh. prepare-release uses chunks too, so the cutover result is the one later refreshes keep.

chunks_of_2000_no_time_limit.note: idle machine; up to 20 s per chunk while other jobs ran

chunks_with_a_6_s_time_limit.rejected: boundaries depend on machine speed, so results differ between runs

chunks_of_1000.rejected: measured under load; each chunk reloads its window, so total time doubled without a shorter longest chunk

measurements.single_vs_chunked_partition: about 2% of items are grouped differently (1,486 from the titles-v4 state); each method is stable on its own output

tests: tests/test_story_refresh_chunks.py: chunks reach the same events as one transaction; the crawl refresh indexes one chunk and leaves a backlog; a chunk past its time commits what it placed; a failed chunk keeps the chunks before it
tests/test_story_merge.py: a reindex in chunks indexes each article once (queue empty, 4 items, 2 chunks); a member 120 h after the root anchor stays when rechecked
8 of 8 mutations are caught: 7 fail a test; removing the bookkeeping of indexed items makes the chunked tests never finish
